workflow_lapses: The invalid PowerShell native-command grouping pattern recurred once after publication and failed before reading or changing state.
The first focused packet expected a generic semantic-hash error where the validator correctly returned the more specific planning-source error.
The first focused packet also found that the plan had not repeated the exact gap_decomposed_not_satisfied result token.
The second focused packet used a literal phrase assertion that did not normalize a Markdown line wrap.
The first broader packet named a nonexistent separate environment-architecture plan test and aborted before collection.
One read-only rg command included a Windows-invalid wildcard path after two explicit valid paths; the corrected directory-scoped search succeeded.
The first clockwork check omitted an exact required next-boundary token and failed closed.

The rejection label was then misread as a count requirement; a semantically useful boundary was added, but the second check rejected until the code-owned required set was inspected and its exact ordinary-practice token added.

While recording the two rejections, the register-summary revision was incorrectly advanced per incident rather than once per tranche; the third check rejected the missing evidence path until revision 637 was restored with the larger incident count.
bounded_conclusion: The tranche did not alter readiness counts, but it converted one composite gap into a finite dependency graph with three immediately actionable repository nodes and an explicit boundary around six real-world facts and five human choices. Nine cheap workflow lapses were contained before publication; none caused a runtime, provider, database, product or protected effect.
